Q9.purpose: Compute click-to-session drop-off for meta paid_social in August vs September 2026

SELECT date_format(to_date(ms.date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
       SUM(ms.clicks) AS clicks,
       SUM(wt.sessions) AS sessions,
       SUM(wt.sessions) / NULLIF(SUM(ms.clicks), 0) AS click_to_session_ratio
FROM WHYDROP_FILES.marketing_spend ms
JOIN WHYDROP_FILES.web_traffic wt
  ON ms.date = wt.date
 AND ms.channel = 'meta'
 AND wt.source = 'paid_social'
WHERE ms.date BETWEEN '2026-08-01' AND '2026-09-30'
  AND ms.channel = 'meta'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

Q16.purpose: Conversion metrics (orders per session) and revenue per session for P001 paid social before vs after the price change
Q16.sql:

  SUM(o.quantity * o.unit_price_usd) AS revenue_usd,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_cnt,

  o.country,
  o.month,
  o.revenue,
  o.orders_cnt,

FROM (
  SELECT
    country,
    date_format(to_date(date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,

    COUNT(*) AS orders_cnt

Q25.purpose: Compare total orders vs sessions (traffic volume) per month to see if clicks held up
Q25.sql:
WITH orders_by_month AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(to_date(date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_cnt
  FROM WHYDROP_FILES.orders
  WHERE channel = 'paid_social'
    AND date >= '2026-08-01'
    AND date < '2026-10-01'
  GROUP BY month
),
sessions_by_month AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(to_date(date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
    SUM(sessions) AS sessions_cnt
  FROM WHYDROP_FILES.web_traffic
  WHERE source = 'paid_social'
    AND date >= '2026-08-01'
    AND date < '2026-10-01'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  o.month,
  o.orders_cnt,
  s.sessions_cnt,
  o.orders_cnt / s.sessions_cnt AS orders_per_session
FROM orders_by_month o
JOIN sessions_by_month s
  ON o.month = s.month
WHERE o.month IN ('2026-08', '2026-09')
ORDER BY o.month

Q26.purpose: Compare revenue per click (revenue divided by ad clicks) for Aug vs Sep
Q26.sql:
WITH revenue_by_month AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(to_date(date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
    SUM(unit_price_usd * quantity) AS total_revenue
  FROM WHYDROP_FILES.orders
  WHERE channel = 'paid_social'
    AND date >= '2026-08-01'
    AND date < '2026-10-01'
  GROUP BY month
),
ad_spend_by_month AS (
  SELECT
    date_format(to_date(date), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
    SUM(clicks) AS clicks,
    SUM(spend_usd) AS spend
  FROM WHYDROP_FILES.marketing_spend
  WHERE channel = 'meta'
    AND date >= '2026-08-01'
    AND date < '2026-10-01'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  r.month,
  r.total_revenue,
  a.clicks,
  a.spend,
  r.total_revenue / a.clicks AS revenue_per_click,
  r.total_revenue / a.spend AS revenue_per_spend
FROM revenue_by_month r
JOIN ad_spend_by_month a
  ON r.month = a.month
WHERE r.month IN ('2026-08', '2026-09')
ORDER BY r.month

memory_recalled.content: [Is our ad spend still working?] REJECTED: Paid social (meta) spend is no longer efficient: cost per click and cost per order have risen while return on ad spend has fallen. - ROAS and cost per order deteriorated sharply, but CPC actually fell slightly, so the specific claim that cost per click rose is contradicted by the data.

[Is our ad spend still working?] VERIFIED CAUSE: Paid social clicks are not reaching the site because landing_404s spiked, so ad spend is wasted on broken landing pages. - Paid social landing 404 errors spiked while orders and revenue collapsed, indicating broken landing pages are wasting spend. (conf 0.93, queries Q1,Q2,Q3)

[Is our ad spend still working?] REJECTED: A recent price increase or product release reduced conversion of paid social traffic, making ad spend look ineffective even though traffic is intact. - Paid social sessions collapsed from August to September while conversion rate slightly increased, so the issue is traffic loss rather than conversion suppression.

[Is our ad spend still working?] REJECTED: Paid social is shifting toward lower-converting geographies or lower-priced products, reducing revenue per click even if clicks and sessions hold up. - Paid social revenue per order and average unit price both rose from August to September while order volume collapsed, so the revenue drop is not explained by a shift to lower-priced products or lower-converting geographies.

[Is our ad spend still working?] REJECTED: Refunds and quality complaints on paid social orders are rising, so customers acquired by ads are not retaining value and spend is effectively wasted. - Paid social refunds fell from $64.00 in August to $12.00 in September and quality-related tickets stayed at zero, so the claim that rising refunds/quality complaints are wasting ad spend is not supported by the data.
